chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man did not purify (pay zakat on) his camels or his sheep for two years, then he sold them on condition that the buyer would purify them for what has passed. He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, its zakat is taken from him, and the seller pursues it with him, or the seller pays its zakat.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the missed zakat on animals when they are sold?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the issue of 'Zakat al-Bahimah' (livestock charity) is clarified for cases of delayed payment upon sale. The Imam establishes that the obligation remains with the original owner (the seller), who may either deduct the amount from the sale price or pay it directly, ensuring the financial liability does not transfer to the buyer unless explicitly agreed. This ruling highlights the principle that zakat is a debt on the wealth owner rather than a property tax attached to the asset itself.

en.hubeali: Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man did not pay Zakāt on his camel or his sheep for two years, Then he sells it stipulating upon the buyer that he would be paying the Zakāt on it on what has passed’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, its Zakāt would be taken from him, and the seller would pursue with it or else the seller would have to pay the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 5. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has not paid Zakat for his camel or sheep for two years then sells to another man who, as part of the deal, is asked to pay its Zakat. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, Zakat is collected from him and the seller pursues him for payment or himself pays its Zakat.’”
